title: North Korean leader receives Philippine ambassador
summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un personally received the credentials of foreign ambassadors, including Philippine Ambassador Jaime FlorCruz, marking the first time in over three decades.

blocks.text: Philippine Ambassador Jaime FlorCruz poses with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un.

MANILA, Philippines — North Korean leader Kim Jong Un personally received the credentials of foreign ambassadors, including Philippine Ambassador Jaime FlorCruz, marking the first time in over three decades.

FlorCruz presented his Letters of Credence to Kim in Pyongyang on Nov. 22, formally assuming his duties as Philippine Ambassador to the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (DPRK), with residence in Beijing.
The ceremony was the first of such kind officiated by Kim since assuming leadership in 2011. FlorCruz joined nine other recently appointed ambassadors at the event.

In his brief speech during the ceremony, Kim hopes the ambassadors will perform their mission and duty to promote confidence building between their respective countries and the DPRK and to strengthen relations of friendship in conformity with mutual interests.
Based in Beijing as the Philippine ambassador to China, FlorCruz is also the non-resident Philippine ambassador to Mongolia and now DPRK.
